name: Cloudflare
tagline: Free static site & Jamstack hosting on Cloudflare's global edge network
description: Cloudflare Pages hosts static and Jamstack sites free on Cloudflare's edge network — fast builds, unlimited bandwidth, but no PHP or WordPress support.
about: Cloudflare is primarily a CDN, DNS and web-security company — its core business is protecting and accelerating other people's websites, not hosting them outright. Cloudflare Pages is its one genuinely hosting-relevant product: a free platform for deploying static sites and Jamstack frontends (built with frameworks like Next.js, Astro, Hugo or plain HTML) directly to Cloudflare's global edge network, with Git-based deploys and preview builds on every pull request.

The free tier allows up to 500 builds per month, one concurrent build, up to 20,000 files per deployment, and unbounded bandwidth and requests for static assets — there's no bandwidth bill regardless of traffic. Custom domains, automatic HTTPS and unlimited sites per account are included at no cost. A paid Workers Paid plan ($5/month) raises the ceiling to 5,000 builds per month and 5 concurrent builds, and is really aimed at projects that also lean on Pages Functions (Cloudflare's serverless compute layer) beyond the free Workers request allowance.

Pages is built for static output only — it does not run PHP, MySQL or a traditional WordPress/cPanel stack, so it's not a drop-in replacement for shared hosting. It fits static marketing sites, documentation, blogs generated by a static-site generator, and Jamstack frontends that call external APIs, but not a database-driven CMS site running server-side PHP.
policies: Cloudflare Pages' free tier has no time limit and requires no credit card to start — it's free indefinitely within the stated build and file limits, not a time-boxed trial.

Paid Cloudflare plans (including Workers Paid, which raises Pages' build limits) are billed monthly and can be cancelled at any time from the Cloudflare dashboard; Cloudflare does not publish a blanket money-back guarantee for its self-serve plans the way traditional hosts do, so check the current terms on cloudflare.com before committing to a paid tier.
